description: Run and analyze a molecular dynamics simulation: build the system, minimize energy, equilibrate, run production, analyze trajectories, validate against experiment, and produce the MD report.

steps.description: Build the simulation system from molecular coordinates, topology, and force field selection.

inputs.name: molecule-structure
inputs.desc: PDB, MOL2, or XYZ coordinate file for the target molecule or system

inputs.name: simulation-goal
inputs.desc: What property or behavior the simulation should investigate

inputs.name: solvent-conditions
inputs.desc: Solvent type, ionic strength, pH, and box dimensions

outputs.name: system-topology
outputs.desc: Complete topology file with atom types, bonds, angles, and dihedrals

outputs.name: force-field-selection
outputs.desc: Chosen force field and parameter justification

outputs.name: initial-coordinates
outputs.desc: Solvated and ionized system coordinates ready for minimization

process: Parse the input structure and assign atom types from the chosen force field
Solvate the system in a periodic box with the specified solvent and add counterions
Validate that all parameters are assigned and no missing terms exist
Write the topology and coordinate files in the simulation engine's format

steps.description: Minimize the system energy to remove steric clashes and bad contacts before dynamics.

inputs.name: system-topology
inputs.desc: Topology file from the system builder

inputs.name: initial-coordinates
inputs.desc: Starting coordinates with solvent and ions

outputs.name: minimized-coordinates
outputs.desc: Energy-minimized structure with no steric clashes

outputs.name: minimization-log
outputs.desc: Energy convergence trace showing steps and final potential energy

process: Run steepest descent minimization until the maximum force drops below the threshold
Switch to conjugate gradient minimization for fine convergence
Check that the final energy is reasonable and no atoms have extreme velocities
Write the minimized coordinates for the equilibration step

steps.description: Equilibrate the system through NVT then NPT ensembles to reach stable temperature and pressure.

inputs.name: minimized-coordinates
inputs.desc: Energy-minimized structure

inputs.name: system-topology
inputs.desc: Topology file

inputs.name: target-conditions
inputs.desc: Target temperature (K) and pressure (bar)

outputs.name: equilibrated-coordinates
outputs.desc: System at stable temperature and pressure, ready for production

outputs.name: equilibration-metrics
outputs.desc: Temperature, pressure, density, and energy traces over the equilibration

process: Run NVT equilibration with position restraints on solute to stabilize temperature
Run NPT equilibration to converge the density and box volume at the target pressure
Check that temperature, pressure, and density have plateaued within acceptable variance
Release restraints gradually and confirm the system remains stable

steps.description: Run the production simulation and collect trajectory frames for analysis.

inputs.name: equilibrated-coordinates
inputs.desc: Equilibrated starting point

inputs.name: system-topology
inputs.desc: Topology file

inputs.name: simulation-goal
inputs.desc: Target property dictating run length and frame output interval

outputs.name: trajectory-file
outputs.desc: Trajectory with coordinates saved at regular intervals

outputs.name: energy-log
outputs.desc: Time series of potential energy, kinetic energy, temperature, and pressure

outputs.name: run-parameters
outputs.desc: Timestep, total time, thermostat, barostat, and output frequency used

process: Configure the production run parameters: timestep, total length, output frequency
Launch the simulation with the chosen thermostat and barostat settings
Monitor for instabilities (energy drift, temperature excursions, box collapse)
Collect the trajectory, energy log, and checkpoint files

steps.description: Analyze the production trajectory for structural, dynamic, and thermodynamic properties.

inputs.name: trajectory-file
inputs.desc: Production trajectory

inputs.name: system-topology
inputs.desc: Topology for atom selection and grouping

inputs.name: simulation-goal
inputs.desc: Which analyses to prioritize

outputs.name: structural-metrics
outputs.desc: RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, secondary structure content over time

outputs.name: interaction-analysis
outputs.desc: Hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, contact maps, and binding free energy estimates

outputs.name: dynamic-properties
outputs.desc: Diffusion coefficients, correlation functions, and relaxation times

process: Compute RMSD and RMSF relative to the starting or average structure
Analyze hydrogen bonds, salt bridges, and hydrophobic contacts over time
Calculate radial distribution functions for solvent and ion interactions
Extract dynamic properties: mean square displacement, autocorrelation functions

steps.description: Compare simulation results against experimental observables to assess accuracy.

inputs.name: structural-metrics
inputs.desc: RMSD, RMSF, and structural data from the trajectory analysis

inputs.name: interaction-analysis
inputs.desc: Computed interaction energies and contacts

inputs.name: experimental-data
inputs.desc: Published or measured experimental values for comparison

outputs.name: validation-report
outputs.desc: Side-by-side comparison of simulated vs experimental values with deviations

outputs.name: md-summary-report
outputs.desc: Complete MD study report covering system setup, protocol, results, and validation

process: Tabulate simulated observables alongside their experimental counterparts
Compute agreement metrics (correlation, RMSE, percent deviation) for each property
Identify where the simulation diverges from experiment and possible causes (force field, sampling, system size)
Write the final report combining methods, results, and validation assessment

description: Analyze sample composition by neutron activation: prepare samples, irradiate, measure gamma spectra, identify isotopes, quantify elemental concentrations, and produce the NAA report.

steps.description: Prepare and encapsulate samples and standards for reactor irradiation.

inputs.name: sample-material
inputs.desc: Description of the sample matrix and expected elements

inputs.name: analysis-goals
inputs.desc: Target elements and required detection limits

outputs.name: prepared-samples
outputs.desc: Weighed, encapsulated samples and certified reference materials ready for irradiation

outputs.name: irradiation-plan
outputs.desc: Reactor position, neutron flux, and irradiation duration for each sample set

process: Dry, homogenize, and weigh the samples into irradiation vials
Select and prepare certified reference materials that bracket the expected concentrations
Calculate the required irradiation time based on target sensitivity and expected activities
Seal and label all vials with sample IDs and positions in the irradiation container

steps.description: Irradiate samples in the reactor and measure gamma spectra at timed decay intervals.

inputs.name: prepared-samples
inputs.desc: Sealed sample and standard vials

inputs.name: irradiation-plan
inputs.desc: Flux position and duration

outputs.name: gamma-spectra
outputs.desc: Measured gamma spectra at each counting interval for all samples and standards

outputs.name: counting-log
outputs.desc: Detector geometry, live time, dead time, and decay time for each measurement

process: Irradiate the sample set at the planned reactor position and neutron flux
After irradiation, allow short-lived isotopes to decay to reduce dead time
Count samples on the HPGe detector at scheduled intervals (short, medium, long decay)
Record live time, dead time, sample-to-detector distance, and spectrum file for each count

steps.description: Identify radioisotopes in the gamma spectra by matching photopeaks to known energies.

inputs.name: gamma-spectra
inputs.desc: Raw gamma spectra from all counting sessions

inputs.name: analysis-goals
inputs.desc: Target element list to guide peak search

outputs.name: peak-assignments
outputs.desc: Each identified photopeak with isotope, energy, net area, and uncertainty

outputs.name: interference-flags
outputs.desc: Peaks where multiple isotopes overlap and require correction

process: Calibrate the energy axis using known calibration sources
Run automatic peak search and fit Gaussian peaks to extract net areas
Match peak energies to the isotope library and assign each peak
Flag spectral interferences where two isotopes contribute to the same energy region

steps.description: Correct for self-shielding, matrix effects, and spectral interferences.

inputs.name: peak-assignments
inputs.desc: Identified peaks with net areas

inputs.name: interference-flags
inputs.desc: Overlapping peak issues

inputs.name: sample-material
inputs.desc: Matrix composition for self-shielding calculation

outputs.name: corrected-activities
outputs.desc: Corrected net activities for each isotope in each sample

outputs.name: correction-factors
outputs.desc: Self-shielding, coincidence summing, and interference correction factors applied

process: Calculate neutron self-shielding factors based on sample mass and composition
Apply coincidence summing corrections for isotopes with cascade gamma emissions
Subtract spectral interference contributions from overlapping peaks
Propagate uncertainties through all correction factors

steps.description: Quantify elemental concentrations by comparing sample activities to standards.

inputs.name: corrected-activities
inputs.desc: Corrected net activities for all samples and standards

inputs.name: counting-log
inputs.desc: Timing and geometry data for decay and efficiency corrections

outputs.name: elemental-concentrations
outputs.desc: Concentration of each element in each sample with uncertainties

outputs.name: quality-metrics
outputs.desc: Detection limits, precision, and accuracy against reference materials

process: Apply the comparator method: ratio sample activity to standard activity with decay corrections
Calculate mass fractions for each element from the activity ratios
Compute detection limits for elements below the quantification threshold
Validate accuracy by comparing measured reference material values to certified values

steps.description: Compile the NAA results into a final analytical report.

inputs.name: elemental-concentrations
inputs.desc: Quantified elements with uncertainties

inputs.name: quality-metrics
inputs.desc: Detection limits and reference material agreement

inputs.name: correction-factors
inputs.desc: All corrections applied during the analysis

outputs.name: naa-report
outputs.desc: Complete NAA report with methods, results tables, QA/QC, and interpretation

outputs.name: data-archive
outputs.desc: Archived spectra, peak fit files, and calculation spreadsheets

process: Organize results into tables by sample with element, concentration, uncertainty, and detection limit
Write the methods section covering irradiation, counting, and correction procedures
Include QA/QC results showing reference material agreement
Archive all raw spectra and intermediate calculations alongside the report

description: Analyze a lidar point cloud: import and register the scan, classify points, generate terrain and surface models, extract features, validate, and produce the analysis report.

steps.description: Import raw lidar data and register multiple scans into a common coordinate system.

inputs.name: raw-lidar-files
inputs.desc: LAS/LAZ files from the lidar sensor or data provider

inputs.name: survey-metadata
inputs.desc: Coordinate reference system, flight lines, and GPS/IMU data

outputs.name: registered-point-cloud
outputs.desc: Merged point cloud in the project coordinate system

outputs.name: registration-quality
outputs.desc: RMS alignment error and overlap statistics between scans

process: Import each scan and verify the point count, extent, and return types
Transform all scans to the project coordinate reference system
Register overlapping scans using ICP or tie-point alignment and record the residuals
Merge into a single point cloud and remove duplicate points in overlap zones

steps.description: Classify each point as ground, vegetation, building, water, noise, or other categories.

inputs.name: registered-point-cloud
inputs.desc: Merged and aligned point cloud

inputs.name: classification-scheme
inputs.desc: ASPRS class codes or custom classes for the project

outputs.name: classified-point-cloud
outputs.desc: Point cloud with class labels assigned to every point

outputs.name: classification-statistics
outputs.desc: Point count and percentage in each class

process: Run ground classification using progressive morphological filtering or cloth simulation
Classify above-ground points into vegetation height strata (low, medium, high)
Identify building footprints from planar surface detection in the above-ground points
Flag noise points (isolated outliers, low-return artifacts) and unclassified points

steps.description: Generate digital terrain model (DTM) and digital surface model (DSM) from classified points.

inputs.name: classified-point-cloud
inputs.desc: Point cloud with ground and surface classes assigned

outputs.name: digital-terrain-model
outputs.desc: Gridded bare-earth elevation model from ground points

outputs.name: digital-surface-model
outputs.desc: Gridded top-of-canopy/structure elevation model from all first returns

outputs.name: normalized-height-model
outputs.desc: Height above ground for every point (DSM minus DTM)

process: Interpolate ground-classified points to a regular grid to create the DTM
Interpolate first-return points to create the DSM at the same grid resolution
Subtract the DTM from the DSM to produce the normalized height model
Fill voids and smooth artifacts at grid boundaries

steps.description: Extract measurable features from the point cloud and derived models.

inputs.name: classified-point-cloud
inputs.desc: Classified points

inputs.name: normalized-height-model
inputs.desc: Height above ground for each point

inputs.name: survey-metadata
inputs.desc: Project goals defining which features to extract

outputs.name: extracted-features
outputs.desc: Canopy height metrics, building footprints, power line clearances, or other requested features

outputs.name: feature-statistics
outputs.desc: Summary statistics for each feature class across the study area

process: Compute canopy height metrics per plot or grid cell (mean, max, percentiles, cover fraction)
Delineate building footprints and estimate roof heights from the classified building points
Measure clearance distances between power lines and vegetation where applicable
Export features as vector polygons, raster grids, or tabular summaries

steps.description: Validate the lidar products against independently measured ground truth.

inputs.name: digital-terrain-model
inputs.desc: DTM to validate

inputs.name: extracted-features
inputs.desc: Extracted features to validate

inputs.name: ground-truth-data
inputs.desc: Field measurements, survey points, or reference datasets

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Error statistics: RMSE, bias, and R-squared for terrain and features

outputs.name: error-map
outputs.desc: Spatial distribution of errors across the study area

process: Match ground truth points to the corresponding DTM cells and extracted feature locations
Compute the signed error (lidar minus ground truth) at each validation point
Calculate summary error statistics: mean error, RMSE, median absolute error, R-squared
Map the spatial pattern of errors to identify systematic biases (slope, land cover, scan angle)

steps.description: Compile the lidar processing results into a final analysis report.

inputs.name: validation-results
inputs.desc: Accuracy assessment statistics

inputs.name: extracted-features
inputs.desc: Final feature datasets

inputs.name: classification-statistics
inputs.desc: Point classification summary

outputs.name: lidar-report
outputs.desc: Complete lidar analysis report with methods, products, accuracy, and deliverables

outputs.name: deliverable-package
outputs.desc: All output rasters, vectors, and point clouds for the client or collaborator

process: Write the methods section covering data acquisition, registration, classification, and feature extraction
Present the products with maps, cross-sections, and summary statistics
Include the accuracy assessment with error statistics and spatial error maps
Package all deliverables with metadata and coordinate system documentation

description: Isolate an active compound from a complex mixture: screen the crude extract, fractionate, track activity through sub-fractions, identify the active compound, and confirm its activity.

steps.description: Screen the crude extract for biological activity to confirm the starting material is active.

inputs.name: crude-extract
inputs.desc: Source material extract (plant, microbial, marine) in a defined solvent

inputs.name: bioassay-protocol
inputs.desc: Target activity assay: antimicrobial, cytotoxic, enzyme inhibition, or other

outputs.name: crude-activity-result
outputs.desc: Activity measurement (IC50, MIC, percent inhibition) for the crude extract

outputs.name: fractionation-decision
outputs.desc: Go/no-go decision and recommended fractionation strategy based on activity level

process: Dissolve the crude extract at a standard concentration series
Run the bioassay with positive and negative controls
Determine the dose-response curve and activity metric
Decide whether the activity warrants fractionation and which method to use

steps.description: Separate the crude extract into primary fractions by polarity or size.

inputs.name: crude-extract
inputs.desc: Active crude extract to fractionate

inputs.name: fractionation-decision
inputs.desc: Recommended method: liquid-liquid partition, flash chromatography, or size exclusion

outputs.name: primary-fractions
outputs.desc: Set of fractions with solvent, mass, and fraction ID

outputs.name: fractionation-log
outputs.desc: Column conditions, solvent gradient, and fraction collection windows

process: Set up the fractionation system (column packing, solvent preparation, gradient program)
Load the crude extract and collect fractions at defined intervals or polarity steps
Evaporate each fraction to dryness and record the recovered mass
Label and store fractions for bioassay testing

steps.description: Test each fraction for activity to identify which ones carry the active compound.

inputs.name: primary-fractions
inputs.desc: Fractions to test

inputs.name: bioassay-protocol
inputs.desc: Same assay used for the crude screen

outputs.name: active-fractions
outputs.desc: Fractions that retain activity above the threshold

outputs.name: activity-map
outputs.desc: Activity plotted against fraction number showing the activity distribution

process: Dissolve each fraction at the test concentration
Run the bioassay on all fractions in parallel with the same controls as the crude screen
Rank fractions by activity level
Select the most active fraction(s) for sub-fractionation

steps.description: Sub-fractionate the active fraction to further purify the active compound.

inputs.name: active-fractions
inputs.desc: Primary fractions with confirmed activity

inputs.name: activity-map
inputs.desc: Activity profile guiding the sub-fractionation strategy

outputs.name: purified-compound
outputs.desc: Isolated compound at the highest achievable purity

outputs.name: purification-log
outputs.desc: HPLC or column conditions, retention times, and purity assessment

process: Select the chromatographic method for sub-fractionation (preparative HPLC, semi-prep)
Optimize the gradient to resolve the active peak from neighboring compounds
Collect the target peak and assess purity by analytical HPLC
Repeat if purity is below 95 percent or if activity splits between sub-fractions

steps.description: Identify the isolated compound by spectroscopic methods (NMR, MS, IR, UV).

inputs.name: purified-compound
inputs.desc: Isolated compound of sufficient purity and mass for spectroscopy

inputs.name: purification-log
inputs.desc: Chromatographic behavior hinting at compound class

outputs.name: structure-assignment
outputs.desc: Proposed molecular structure with supporting spectral data

outputs.name: spectral-data-package
outputs.desc: NMR, MS, IR, and UV spectra with peak assignments

process: Acquire high-resolution mass spectrum to determine the molecular formula
Record 1D and 2D NMR spectra (1H, 13C, COSY, HSQC, HMBC) and assign peaks
Use IR and UV data to confirm functional groups and chromophores
Compare against databases and literature to confirm or propose the structure

steps.description: Confirm the biological activity of the pure compound and compare to the crude extract.

inputs.name: purified-compound
inputs.desc: Structurally identified pure compound

inputs.name: bioassay-protocol
inputs.desc: Same assay as the original screen

inputs.name: crude-activity-result
inputs.desc: Original crude extract activity for comparison

outputs.name: confirmed-activity
outputs.desc: Dose-response curve and potency metric for the pure compound

outputs.name: fractionation-report
outputs.desc: Complete bioassay-guided fractionation report from crude to pure compound

process: Run a full dose-response curve with the pure compound
Compare potency (IC50, MIC) to the crude extract to assess enrichment
Test for cytotoxicity or selectivity if relevant to the application
Write the final report covering the fractionation path, structure, and confirmed activity

description: Build an age-depth model for a sediment or ice core: compile dated horizons, calibrate, select the modeling approach, run the model, and produce the chronology.

steps.description: Compile all dated horizons from the core including radiocarbon, tephra, and paleomagnetic tie points.

inputs.name: core-log
inputs.desc: Core description with depths, lithology, and sampling locations

inputs.name: dating-results
inputs.desc: Raw dating results: radiocarbon ages, tephra IDs, paleomagnetic reversals, other markers

outputs.name: dated-horizons-table
outputs.desc: Table of all dated points: depth, age, uncertainty, dating method, and material dated

outputs.name: outlier-candidates
outputs.desc: Dates flagged as potential outliers based on stratigraphic inversion or large uncertainty

process: Enter each date with its depth, reported age, uncertainty, and method
Check for stratigraphic inversions (younger dates below older dates)
Flag dates on reworked material or with anomalously large uncertainties
Add any event horizons (tephra layers, paleomagnetic boundaries) with their known ages

steps.description: Calibrate radiocarbon ages to calendar years using the appropriate calibration curve.

inputs.name: dated-horizons-table
inputs.desc: Raw dates including radiocarbon ages to calibrate

inputs.name: calibration-curve
inputs.desc: IntCal20, SHCal20, or Marine20 depending on sample origin

outputs.name: calibrated-dates
outputs.desc: Calendar age probability distributions for each radiocarbon date

outputs.name: reservoir-corrections
outputs.desc: Any marine or freshwater reservoir corrections applied

process: Select the calibration curve based on hemisphere and sample environment
Apply reservoir corrections for marine or freshwater samples if needed
Calibrate each radiocarbon age to produce the calendar age probability distribution
Record the median, 1-sigma, and 2-sigma calendar age ranges

steps.description: Select the age-depth modeling approach based on the dating density and core type.

inputs.name: calibrated-dates
inputs.desc: Calibrated calendar age distributions

inputs.name: outlier-candidates
inputs.desc: Flagged potential outliers

inputs.name: core-log
inputs.desc: Lithology and sedimentation context

outputs.name: model-configuration
outputs.desc: Chosen model (Bacon, OxCal, clam, linear interpolation) with parameter settings

outputs.name: outlier-decisions
outputs.desc: Which flagged dates to include, downweight, or exclude and why

process: Assess dating density and decide if a Bayesian approach is justified
Choose the model: Bacon for flexible accumulation, OxCal for sequence models, clam for simple cases
Set model parameters: section thickness, accumulation rate prior, memory strength
Decide on outlier treatment: exclude, downweight, or model with an outlier probability

steps.description: Run the age-depth model and extract the chronology with confidence intervals.

inputs.name: calibrated-dates
inputs.desc: Input dates for the model

inputs.name: model-configuration
inputs.desc: Model type and parameters

inputs.name: outlier-decisions
inputs.desc: Outlier handling instructions

outputs.name: age-depth-model
outputs.desc: Median age and 95% confidence interval at every depth increment

outputs.name: accumulation-rate
outputs.desc: Sedimentation rate profile with uncertainty over the core length

process: Run the model with the configured parameters (MCMC iterations for Bayesian models)
Check convergence diagnostics (trace plots, Gelman-Rubin statistic)
Extract the median age and 95% credible interval at each depth step
Compute the sediment accumulation rate as the inverse of the age-depth slope

steps.description: Produce the final chronology report with the age-depth plot and supporting data.

inputs.name: age-depth-model
inputs.desc: Final age model with confidence intervals

inputs.name: accumulation-rate
inputs.desc: Sedimentation rate profile

inputs.name: dated-horizons-table
inputs.desc: Original dated horizons for display on the plot

outputs.name: chronology-report
outputs.desc: Report including the age-depth plot, accumulation rates, methods, and data tables

outputs.name: age-model-output-file
outputs.desc: Machine-readable file of depth vs age for use in proxy interpretation

process: Generate the age-depth plot with dated horizons, median model, and 95% envelope
Plot the sedimentation rate profile with uncertainty bands
Write the methods section documenting model choice, parameters, and outlier handling
Export the age model as a table and file for downstream proxy-age assignment

description: Analyze a rock thin section: examine under plane and cross-polarized light, identify minerals, classify the rock, interpret petrogenesis, and produce the petrographic report.

steps.description: Examine the thin section under plane-polarized light to record color, relief, cleavage, and texture.

inputs.name: thin-section
inputs.desc: Polished thin section mounted on a glass slide

inputs.name: sample-context
inputs.desc: Field location, hand sample description, and geological setting

outputs.name: ppl-observations
outputs.desc: Mineral colors, relief, crystal habit, cleavage, and textural relationships under PPL

outputs.name: texture-description
outputs.desc: Rock texture: grain size, shape, sorting, fabric, and any deformation features

process: Scan the entire section at low magnification to note the overall texture and mineral distribution
Record each mineral phase: color, pleochroism, relief, crystal form, and cleavage
Document the texture: equigranular vs porphyritic, foliated vs massive, grain boundaries
Note any alteration, veining, inclusions, or accessory phases

steps.description: Examine under cross-polarized light to record birefringence, extinction, and twinning for mineral identification.

inputs.name: thin-section
inputs.desc: Same thin section

inputs.name: ppl-observations
inputs.desc: PPL observations to correlate with XPL behavior

outputs.name: xpl-observations
outputs.desc: Birefringence colors, extinction angle and type, twinning, and interference figures for each phase

outputs.name: mineral-candidates
outputs.desc: Preliminary mineral identifications based on combined PPL and XPL properties

process: Record the maximum birefringence color for each mineral phase
Determine extinction type (parallel, inclined, symmetrical) and measure the angle where possible
Identify twinning patterns (simple, polysynthetic, cross-hatch) diagnostic of specific minerals
Obtain interference figures (uniaxial vs biaxial, optic sign) for ambiguous phases

steps.description: Confirm the mineral assemblage by integrating PPL and XPL observations with diagnostic criteria.

inputs.name: ppl-observations
inputs.desc: Plane-polarized light data

inputs.name: xpl-observations
inputs.desc: Cross-polarized light data

inputs.name: mineral-candidates
inputs.desc: Preliminary identifications to confirm

outputs.name: confirmed-minerals
outputs.desc: Final mineral list with volume percentages estimated by point counting or visual estimate

outputs.name: modal-composition
outputs.desc: Quantitative or semi-quantitative mineral proportions

process: Compare each candidate mineral's properties against determinative tables
Resolve ambiguities using distinguishing criteria (e.g., feldspar twinning, pyroxene cleavage angles)
Estimate modal proportions by visual comparison charts or point counting
List the mineral assemblage in order of abundance

steps.description: Classify the rock using the mineral assemblage, texture, and appropriate classification scheme.

inputs.name: confirmed-minerals
inputs.desc: Identified minerals and proportions

inputs.name: texture-description
inputs.desc: Texture data from PPL examination

inputs.name: sample-context
inputs.desc: Geological setting for context

outputs.name: rock-name
outputs.desc: Formal rock name using the IUGS or appropriate classification scheme

outputs.name: classification-rationale
outputs.desc: The classification diagram or criteria used and where the sample plots

process: Determine if the rock is igneous, metamorphic, or sedimentary based on texture and mineralogy
Apply the appropriate classification: QAPF for plutonic, TAS for volcanic, metamorphic facies, or sedimentary
Plot the modal composition on the relevant diagram to assign the rock name
Note any prefix modifiers (e.g., biotite granite, garnet-bearing amphibolite)

steps.description: Interpret the rock's origin and history from the mineral assemblage, textures, and geological context.

inputs.name: rock-name
inputs.desc: Classified rock name

inputs.name: confirmed-minerals
inputs.desc: Mineral assemblage

inputs.name: texture-description
inputs.desc: Textural evidence

inputs.name: sample-context
inputs.desc: Field relationships and regional geology

outputs.name: petrogenetic-interpretation
outputs.desc: Interpreted formation conditions, source, and subsequent history

outputs.name: petrographic-report
outputs.desc: Complete petrographic report with descriptions, photomicrographs, classification, and interpretation

process: Infer formation conditions from the mineral assemblage (P-T range, melt composition, metamorphic grade)
Interpret the textural sequence: crystallization order, deformation events, alteration stages
Relate the petrography to the regional geological context and tectonic setting
Write the final report with annotated photomicrographs, mineral table, classification, and interpretation

description: Characterize an electrode for electrochemistry: cyclic voltammetry, surface area, impedance spectroscopy, stability testing, and produce the electrode performance report.

steps.description: Measure cyclic voltammograms at multiple scan rates to characterize the electrode's redox behavior.

inputs.name: electrode-setup
inputs.desc: Working electrode, counter electrode, reference electrode, and electrolyte composition

inputs.name: scan-parameters
inputs.desc: Potential window, scan rates (mV/s), and number of cycles

outputs.name: cv-data
outputs.desc: Current-voltage curves at each scan rate with peak positions and currents

outputs.name: redox-characterization
outputs.desc: Peak potentials, peak separation, reversibility assessment, and scan rate dependence

process: Set up the three-electrode cell and purge with inert gas if needed
Record CVs at the lowest scan rate first, increasing through the series
Identify anodic and cathodic peak potentials and currents at each scan rate
Assess reversibility from peak separation and the peak current vs square root of scan rate plot

steps.description: Determine the electroactive surface area from capacitance or redox probe measurements.

inputs.name: cv-data
inputs.desc: Cyclic voltammetry data from the scan rate study

inputs.name: electrode-setup
inputs.desc: Electrode geometry and electrolyte

outputs.name: surface-area
outputs.desc: Electroactive surface area in cm-squared and roughness factor relative to geometric area

outputs.name: surface-area-method
outputs.desc: Method used (double-layer capacitance, Randles-Sevcik with a known redox probe)

process: For capacitance method: measure charging current at multiple scan rates in non-faradaic region
Plot current vs scan rate and extract the double-layer capacitance from the slope
Convert capacitance to area using the standard specific capacitance for the material
For Randles-Sevcik: use peak current vs scan rate slope with a standard redox probe of known diffusion coefficient

steps.description: Run electrochemical impedance spectroscopy and fit an equivalent circuit model.

inputs.name: electrode-setup
inputs.desc: Cell configuration and electrolyte

inputs.name: eis-parameters
inputs.desc: Frequency range, AC amplitude, and DC bias potential

outputs.name: eis-spectra
outputs.desc: Nyquist and Bode plots of impedance vs frequency

outputs.name: equivalent-circuit
outputs.desc: Best-fit circuit model with element values (Rs, Rct, Cdl, Warburg, CPE)

process: Set the DC bias to the open circuit potential or a potential of interest
Sweep frequency from high (100 kHz) to low (10 mHz) with a small AC perturbation
Plot the Nyquist diagram and identify semicircles, linear regions, and their physical meaning
Fit an equivalent circuit model and report the charge transfer resistance, double-layer capacitance, and diffusion parameters

steps.description: Assess the electrode's stability over extended cycling or constant operation.

inputs.name: electrode-setup
inputs.desc: Cell configuration

inputs.name: cv-data
inputs.desc: Baseline CV for comparison after aging

outputs.name: stability-data
outputs.desc: Current or signal retention over time or cycle number

outputs.name: degradation-analysis
outputs.desc: Rate of signal loss, failure mode identification, and operational lifetime estimate

process: Run chronoamperometry at a fixed potential for the target duration
Alternatively run many CV cycles and compare the first and last cycles
Calculate the percent retention of peak current or response signal
Identify degradation modes: fouling, dissolution, structural damage, electrolyte decomposition

steps.description: Compile all electrochemical data into a performance report for the electrode.

inputs.name: redox-characterization
inputs.desc: CV results

inputs.name: surface-area
inputs.desc: Electroactive surface area

inputs.name: equivalent-circuit
inputs.desc: EIS fit results

inputs.name: stability-data
inputs.desc: Long-term stability data

outputs.name: electrode-report
outputs.desc: Complete electrode characterization report with figures, tables, and performance summary

outputs.name: performance-metrics
outputs.desc: Key metrics: sensitivity, linear range, detection limit, response time, stability

process: Assemble the CV, EIS, and stability figures with consistent formatting
Tabulate the key performance metrics and compare against literature benchmarks
Identify the limiting factors for electrode performance
Write the report covering preparation, characterization, results, and recommendations

description: Analyze pollen assemblages from a sediment core: prepare samples, count and identify pollen, compute statistics, build the pollen diagram, interpret vegetation and climate, and produce the palynological report.

steps.description: Process sediment samples to extract and concentrate pollen grains for microscopy.

inputs.name: core-samples
inputs.desc: Sediment subsamples at defined depth intervals from the core

inputs.name: preparation-protocol
inputs.desc: Chemical treatment sequence (HCl, HF, acetolysis, heavy liquid) based on sediment type

outputs.name: prepared-slides
outputs.desc: Mounted slides with concentrated pollen residue and exotic marker grains

outputs.name: preparation-log
outputs.desc: Sample weights, volumes of exotic marker added, and processing notes

process: Add a known number of exotic marker grains (Lycopodium or Eucalyptus) to each sample for concentration calculations
Dissolve carbonates with HCl and silicates with HF as needed
Run acetolysis to remove cellulose and darken pollen walls for easier identification
Mount the residue on slides in glycerol jelly or silicone oil

steps.description: Count pollen grains under the microscope and identify each to the lowest possible taxonomic level.

inputs.name: prepared-slides
inputs.desc: Slides with concentrated pollen

inputs.name: reference-collection
inputs.desc: Pollen morphology keys and reference slides for the study region

outputs.name: pollen-counts
outputs.desc: Raw counts of each pollen taxon per sample with a minimum of 300 terrestrial grains

outputs.name: identification-notes
outputs.desc: Difficult identifications, damaged grains, and non-pollen palynomorphs noted

process: Scan traverse lines across the slide at 400x magnification
Identify each pollen grain using morphological features: aperture type and number, wall structure, size, shape
Count until at least 300 terrestrial pollen grains are reached per sample
Record non-pollen palynomorphs (spores, algae, charcoal) encountered during counting

steps.description: Convert raw counts to percentages and concentrations for each taxon.

inputs.name: pollen-counts
inputs.desc: Raw counts per taxon per sample

inputs.name: preparation-log
inputs.desc: Exotic marker counts and sample volumes for concentration calculation

outputs.name: pollen-percentages
outputs.desc: Each taxon as a percentage of the total terrestrial pollen sum per sample

outputs.name: pollen-concentrations
outputs.desc: Grains per cubic centimeter for each taxon calculated from the exotic marker ratio

process: Define the pollen sum (typically terrestrial pollen, excluding aquatics and spores)
Calculate the percentage of each taxon relative to the pollen sum
Calculate concentrations using the ratio of counted pollen to counted exotic markers
If an age model exists, calculate pollen accumulation rates (grains per cm-squared per year)

steps.description: Build the pollen diagram showing taxon percentages or concentrations plotted against depth or age.

inputs.name: pollen-percentages
inputs.desc: Percentage data for all taxa and samples

inputs.name: core-samples
inputs.desc: Depth information for each sample

outputs.name: pollen-diagram
outputs.desc: Standard pollen diagram with taxa grouped by vegetation type (trees, shrubs, herbs)

outputs.name: pollen-zones
outputs.desc: Statistically or visually defined pollen zones marking assemblage changes

process: Order taxa by ecological group: trees and shrubs (AP), herbs (NAP), aquatics, spores
Plot each taxon as a silhouette or bar against the depth/age axis
Apply zonation (CONISS or visual) to identify boundaries between distinct assemblages
Add the total pollen concentration and charcoal curves as summary tracks

steps.description: Interpret the pollen zones in terms of vegetation change and inferred climate conditions.

inputs.name: pollen-diagram
inputs.desc: Completed pollen diagram with zones

inputs.name: pollen-zones
inputs.desc: Zone boundaries and their defining taxa

inputs.name: sample-context
inputs.desc: Regional vegetation, climate, and archaeological or geological context

outputs.name: vegetation-reconstruction
outputs.desc: Reconstructed vegetation for each zone with dominant communities described

outputs.name: climate-inference
outputs.desc: Inferred climate conditions (temperature, moisture) for each zone based on indicator taxa

process: Describe the vegetation assemblage in each zone using modern analogue comparisons
Identify key indicator taxa for climate inference (e.g., thermophilous trees, steppe herbs)
Correlate zone boundaries with known climate events, archaeological phases, or disturbance history
Assess the role of human impact vs climate as drivers of vegetation change

steps.description: Write the complete palynological report with the diagram, interpretation, and data tables.

inputs.name: pollen-diagram
inputs.desc: Final diagram

inputs.name: vegetation-reconstruction
inputs.desc: Zone-by-zone vegetation description

inputs.name: climate-inference
inputs.desc: Climate interpretations

outputs.name: palynology-report
outputs.desc: Complete report including methods, diagram, interpretation, and raw data appendix

outputs.name: pollen-data-archive
outputs.desc: Raw and processed pollen data in a standard format for repository submission

process: Write the methods covering sampling, preparation, counting, and statistical procedures
Present the pollen diagram with zone descriptions and photomicrographs of key taxa
Discuss the vegetation and climate history in the context of regional records
Format the raw data for archival in a palynological database (European Pollen Database, Neotoma)

description: Monitor structural integrity with acoustic emission: install sensors, acquire data, filter and locate events, classify by waveform, assess damage severity, and produce the AE report.

steps.description: Install acoustic emission sensors on the structure and verify coupling quality.

inputs.name: structure-description
inputs.desc: Geometry, material, and loading conditions of the test article

inputs.name: monitoring-objectives
inputs.desc: What damage or defect types to detect and the coverage area

outputs.name: sensor-layout
outputs.desc: Sensor positions, types, coupling media, and preamplifier gains

outputs.name: coupling-verification
outputs.desc: Pencil lead break test results confirming adequate sensitivity at each sensor

process: Select sensor type and frequency range based on the material and expected source mechanisms
Determine sensor positions for source location coverage using the structure's wave velocity
Mount sensors with appropriate couplant and secure them against vibration
Perform pencil lead break tests at each sensor and at mid-points to verify sensitivity and wave speed

steps.description: Acquire acoustic emission signals during loading and record waveforms with timing data.

inputs.name: sensor-layout
inputs.desc: Installed sensor configuration

inputs.name: acquisition-parameters
inputs.desc: Threshold, hit definition time, peak definition time, and sampling rate

outputs.name: raw-ae-data
outputs.desc: Recorded AE hits with waveforms, timestamps, amplitudes, durations, and energy

outputs.name: load-history
outputs.desc: Synchronized load or stress data for correlation with AE activity

process: Set the amplitude threshold above the background noise floor
Configure hit definition timing parameters to separate discrete events
Begin loading the structure and record AE data synchronized with the load signal
Monitor hit rates in real time to detect sudden increases indicating damage onset

steps.description: Filter noise from genuine AE events and locate the sources on the structure.

inputs.name: raw-ae-data
inputs.desc: All recorded hits

inputs.name: sensor-layout
inputs.desc: Sensor positions and measured wave velocities

outputs.name: located-events
outputs.desc: AE events with computed source coordinates and location accuracy estimates

outputs.name: noise-rejected
outputs.desc: Hits classified as electromagnetic interference, friction, or mechanical noise

process: Apply amplitude, duration, and frequency filters to remove obvious noise hits
Use arrival time differences between sensors to compute source locations (triangulation)
Discard events that do not meet the minimum sensor trigger criterion for valid location
Map located events onto the structure geometry

steps.description: Classify AE events by their waveform parameters to distinguish source mechanisms.

inputs.name: located-events
inputs.desc: Filtered and located AE events with waveforms

inputs.name: monitoring-objectives
inputs.desc: Expected damage types for classification categories

outputs.name: classified-events
outputs.desc: Events labeled by source mechanism: matrix cracking, delamination, fiber breakage, friction, etc.

outputs.name: classification-statistics
outputs.desc: Event counts and energy by class over time and load level

process: Extract waveform features: peak amplitude, rise time, duration, frequency centroid, counts
Apply pattern recognition (k-means, supervised classification, or decision boundaries) to group events
Assign physical meaning to each cluster based on known waveform signatures for the material
Track the evolution of each class with increasing load

steps.description: Assess damage severity using AE intensity analysis and load history correlation.

inputs.name: classified-events
inputs.desc: Events with source mechanism labels

inputs.name: load-history
inputs.desc: Applied load or stress over time

inputs.name: classification-statistics
inputs.desc: Cumulative event and energy data by class

outputs.name: severity-assessment
outputs.desc: Damage severity rating based on AE intensity, Kaiser effect, and Felicity ratio

outputs.name: ae-monitoring-report
outputs.desc: Complete AE report with setup, data, analysis, damage assessment, and recommendations

process: Calculate cumulative AE energy and event count as functions of load
Evaluate the Kaiser effect: check whether AE resumes below the previous maximum load (Felicity ratio < 1 indicates damage)
Compute AE intensity (log of cumulative signal strength divided by area) for severity grading
Write the monitoring report covering the test setup, loading protocol, AE results, damage assessment, and structural recommendations

description: Use stable isotopes to study ecological relationships: collect tissue samples, measure isotope ratios, construct the isotopic niche, compute trophic position, map the food web, and produce the isotope ecology report.

steps.description: Collect and prepare tissue samples from organisms across trophic levels for isotope analysis.

inputs.name: study-design
inputs.desc: Target species, trophic levels, sample sizes, and tissue types to collect

inputs.name: site-description
inputs.desc: Habitat type, location, and baseline resource characterization

outputs.name: tissue-samples
outputs.desc: Dried, ground tissue samples with species, tissue type, and collection metadata

outputs.name: baseline-samples
outputs.desc: Primary producer and primary consumer samples for baseline isotope values

process: Collect tissue samples from organisms at each target trophic level (producers, herbivores, predators)
Select the tissue type appropriate for the time scale of interest (muscle, liver, blood, feathers)
Dry samples at 60 degrees C, grind to a fine powder, and weigh aliquots into tin capsules
Include baseline organisms (e.g., filter feeders, primary producers) for trophic position calculation

steps.description: Measure stable isotope ratios (delta-13C, delta-15N, and optionally delta-2H, delta-34S) by mass spectrometry.

inputs.name: tissue-samples
inputs.desc: Prepared sample capsules

inputs.name: baseline-samples
inputs.desc: Baseline organism capsules

outputs.name: isotope-values
outputs.desc: Delta values for each sample with analytical precision (from replicate standards)

outputs.name: quality-control
outputs.desc: Standard reference material results showing accuracy and precision of the run

process: Combust samples in the elemental analyzer coupled to the isotope ratio mass spectrometer
Measure delta-13C and delta-15N for all samples with interspersed reference standards
Correct raw delta values to the international scale using two-point normalization
Assess precision from replicate standards and flag any outlier measurements

steps.description: Construct the isotopic niche space for each species or group using bivariate isotope data.

inputs.name: isotope-values
inputs.desc: Delta-13C and delta-15N values for all samples

outputs.name: isotopic-niches
outputs.desc: Standard ellipse areas (SEA) and convex hull areas for each species or group

outputs.name: niche-overlap-matrix
outputs.desc: Pairwise overlap between species niches in isotope space

process: Plot delta-13C vs delta-15N for each species in bivariate isotope space
Compute standard ellipse areas corrected for sample size (SEAc) using Bayesian estimation
Calculate convex hull total area as a measure of population-level niche width
Compute pairwise niche overlap as the proportion of one species' ellipse inside another's

steps.description: Calculate the trophic position of each consumer relative to the isotopic baseline.

inputs.name: isotope-values
inputs.desc: Consumer delta-15N values

inputs.name: baseline-samples
inputs.desc: Baseline organism isotope values

inputs.name: study-design
inputs.desc: Trophic discrimination factors to apply

outputs.name: trophic-positions
outputs.desc: Estimated trophic position for each consumer species with uncertainty

outputs.name: food-chain-length
outputs.desc: Maximum trophic position observed in the food web

process: Determine the baseline delta-15N from primary consumers or a two-source baseline model
Apply the trophic discrimination factor (typically 3.4 per mil per trophic level for delta-15N)
Calculate trophic position: TP = baseline_trophic_level + (delta-15N_consumer minus delta-15N_baseline) / discrimination_factor
Propagate uncertainty from baseline variability and discrimination factor estimates

steps.description: Map the food web structure from isotope data showing energy flow pathways.

inputs.name: trophic-positions
inputs.desc: Trophic level estimates for each species

inputs.name: isotopic-niches
inputs.desc: Niche positions showing carbon source use

inputs.name: niche-overlap-matrix
inputs.desc: Overlap between species indicating shared resources

outputs.name: food-web-diagram
outputs.desc: Visual food web with species positioned by delta-13C (x) and trophic position (y)

outputs.name: dietary-overlap-analysis
outputs.desc: Which species share resources and the degree of competition implied

process: Position each species on a biplot with delta-13C on the x-axis (carbon source) and trophic position on the y-axis
Draw links between consumers and likely prey based on isotopic mixing model outputs or literature diet data
Identify the dominant energy channels (e.g., pelagic vs benthic, C3 vs C4)
Highlight species with high dietary overlap that may compete for resources

steps.description: Produce the stable isotope ecology report with the food web, niche analyses, and interpretation.

inputs.name: food-web-diagram
inputs.desc: Mapped food web

inputs.name: isotopic-niches
inputs.desc: Species niche metrics

inputs.name: trophic-positions
inputs.desc: Trophic level estimates

inputs.name: dietary-overlap-analysis
inputs.desc: Competition and resource partitioning analysis

outputs.name: isotope-ecology-report
outputs.desc: Complete report covering sampling, analytical methods, food web, niche analysis, and ecological interpretation

outputs.name: isotope-data-archive
outputs.desc: Raw isotope data formatted for repository submission

process: Write the methods covering sampling design, laboratory procedures, and statistical analyses
Present the food web, niche plots, trophic position estimates, and overlap analysis
Discuss the ecological implications: energy flow, resource partitioning, food chain length, keystone roles
Format the raw data for archival in a public data repository
